THOUGHT: This 17-year-old male presents with mucocutaneous bleeding (persistent post-extraction gingival oozing and easy bruising) and a positive family history of similar bleeding, easy bruising, and joint swelling — notably in a male uncle. The joint swelling in the uncle is highly suggestive of hemophilic arthropathy, pointing toward an X-linked recessive coagulopathy. Laboratory findings show a normal platelet count (160,000/mm³), normal PT (15 sec), but markedly prolonged PTT (60 sec), normal bleeding time (6 min — upper limit of normal is ~10 min, so not significantly prolonged), and normal fibrin split products and peripheral smear. The isolated PTT prolongation with normal PT strongly suggests deficiency in the intrinsic pathway (factors VIII, IX, XI, or XII) or presence of an inhibitor (e.g., factor VIII inhibitor). Given age, sex, family history (affected male relative, no affected females mentioned — consistent with X-linked inheritance), and clinical phenotype (mucocutaneous bleeding + post-traumatic/surgical bleeding + family history of joint swelling), hemophilia A (factor VIII deficiency) is far more likely than hemophilia B (factor IX), though both are possible. Hemophilia A is ~5x more common than B. Factor XI deficiency is autosomal recessive and typically less severe, with less prominent joint involvement; the family history (uncle affected, no mention of consanguinity or affected sisters) makes X-linked more plausible. Von Willebrand disease (vWD) is also common and can present with mucocutaneous bleeding and prolonged PTT, but bleeding time is often prolonged (here it’s only 6 min — borderline but not clearly abnormal), and vWD is autosomal dominant with variable penetrance; however, joint swelling is atypical for vWD and more characteristic of hemophilia. The normal platelet count and absence of petechiae further argue against primary platelet disorders. The prolonged PTT with normal PT and platelets, plus X-linked family history and target organ (joint) involvement in the uncle, strongly supports hemophilia A.

DIAGNOSIS: Hemophilia A
